newsitem.title: UK: Infobank shares set first-day premium.
newsitem.headline: Infobank shares set first-day premium.

text.p: Shares in Infobank International Holdings Plc, a provider of electronic commerce systems, set a 15 percent premium on their first day of trade on the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) on Tuesday.
By 1045 GMT shares in the company were quoted at 144p, ahead of their 125p issue price, although no trade was recorded in the stock.

Infobank, which said it was Microsoft's fifth largest authorised supplier to large corporate clients in the UK, is currently piloting an electronic commerce intranet with British Gas Transco, Microsoft and Compaq.
David Fraser, chairman, said the float, which followed several recent hi-tech IPOs, had been well received by investors.

"We have had a very positive response from potential investors, who have recognised that we are not another company dependent on new technology for success, but a company determined to make supply chain management more cost effective using contemporary technologies," Fraser said in a statement.
Infobank also said it was in talks with other major suppliers in the UK and other parts of Europe interested in its electronic commerce systems technology.
The placing raised 7.5 million stg net for the company, valuing it at 24.0 million stg.
